judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary or convenient to the effectuation of the authorized purposes of the commission' is broad, but the provision is a permissive authorisation to convey 'in accordance with the laws of the respective parties'. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contemplates voluntary transfer of signatory property, complementing 14.14(a)'s exclusion of signatory property from condemnation. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Notwithstanding any contrary provision of law' overrides all state and local law by compact, a striking reach, and 'upon the commission's request' plus 'authorized and empowered' leaves unclear whether the political subdivision must convey or merely may. That may/must ambiguity is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It empowers subdivisions to convey notwithstanding contrary law, while 1.5 promises to preserve existing agency functions and New York § 636 requires municipalities to comply with general laws on grants and contracts. Those pull against the 'notwithstanding' clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not in any event exceed the expenditure required to serve the public convenience and necessity' caps the commission's relocation cost by an undefined and famously elastic utility-law phrase, while the relocation cost is otherwise to be paid 'in accordance with the law of the state'. The cap and the state-law rule can produce different numbers, leaving a gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It leaves unstated who bears any excess over the cap, and 14.14(c) makes the commission alone liable for condemnation awards while no provision allocates the relocation shortfall. That gap is specific.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Permission is hereby granted' followed by 'subject to such reasonable conditions as the highway department of the signatory party may require' — the grant is self-executing but conditioned on a 'reasonable' standard controlled by the other side. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It grants rights of way over streets 'now or hereafter owned, opened or dedicated', which overlaps 14.14's condemnation power and 14.15(c)'s relocation rules without stating priority. Moderate-low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Violates or attempts or conspires to violate any provision of this compact or any rule, regulation or order' is criminal in effect yet keyed to the compact's many open-textured provisions, and 'punishable as may be provided by statute of any of the signatory parties within which the offense is committed' leaves the offence's content to five different bodies of law. The vagueness matters far more in a penal provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reach depends on 14.2's rules, 3.8's approval requirement and 6.2(a)'s merely 'recommended' standards — it is unclear whether violating a recommended standard is punishable. That interaction is a genuine construction problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Only to the extent and subject to the procedures prescribed by law generally with respect to officers, agents and employees of the government of the United States' is a compressed reference to the Federal Tort Claims Act without naming it, and 'law generally' is indeterminate. A claimant would have to litigate what body of law is meant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(m) directs that for purposes of the FTCA statutes (28 U.S.C. ch. 171 and § 1346(b)) 'the commission shall not be considered a Federal agency' — so this section borrows a procedure that the reservation says does not apply to the commission. That is a specific, named conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A saving clause using the triple formula 'affecting or intending to affect or in any way to interfere with'; broad but its direction is unmistakable. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves state riparian law while 3.3 empowers allocation under equitable apportionment, 10.3-10.5 impose permits on withdrawals, and 10.8 supersedes state permits — regulation of withdrawals inevitably affects riparian rights. That is a real whole-instrument tension a riparian owner would press.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Amendments and supplements... to implement the purposes thereof' limits amendments by an undefined purposive test, and 'concurred in by all of the others' does not say how concurrence is expressed. Modest but nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(q) reserves to Congress 'the right to alter, amend, or repeal this Act', and 1.4 recognises Congress's power to modify the terms unilaterally — so the compact contains both a unanimity amendment rule and a unilateral federal amendment power. The 1997 and 2007 endnotes show Congress in fact amending without the states' concurrence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'It is the legislative intent that the provisions of such compact be reasonably and liberally construed' pairs two adverbs that can pull apart, and the section supplies no guidance on what liberal construction means for a jurisdictional grant. In any fight over the compact's reach, both sides would cite this sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The liberal-construction directive is invoked to widen 1.2(g) and 3.8, while 1.5, 5.5, 11.1(c), 11.2(c) and 14.19 all counsel narrow readings that preserve existing authority — the instrument thus contains an interpretive instruction at war with its own savings clauses. That is exactly the kind of tension a court must resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Thirty days after the enactment of concurring legislation' by five named parties is a precise trigger, and the execution and filing mechanics are concrete. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: New York § 2 directs that the compact become effective 'in accordance with the provisions of subdivision twenty-one of section fourteen of article fourteen' — i.e., Section 14.21, the severability clause — when the effective-date provision is 14.22. The state enactment mis-cites this section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory stem tying the reservations to Section 1.4. Nothing on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes federal consent conditional on twenty-one reservations, several of which override named compact sections (2.2, 2.4, 2.6, 3.7, 8.4, 11.5) — the stem is the hinge for all of that cross-cutting. Real but deliberate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is corrupted — 'beyond the planning stage untilC' and 'includingC' are plainly garbled — and 'beyond the planning stage' is itself an undefined boundary for a prohibition of great consequence. The 'other than a project for which State supplied funds only will be used' carve-out is also awkwardly placed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bars the commission from carrying out any 'project (as defined in such compact)' without an Act of Congress, which cuts across 3.6(a), 4.1, 6.1, 9.2 and 12.1's grants of project powers, and its scope turns on the same contested 1.2(g) definition. The 'notwithstanding any provision' opener is what keeps it coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Impose any change for water withdrawals' is a clear typographical error for 'charge' — a mechanical mistake in the operative verb of a prohibition. 'Could lawfully have been made without charge on the effective date' also requires a 1961 factual baseline that is now hard to establish.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts back Section 3.7's rate-setting power expressly, and interacts with 3.5(b), 4.3 and 11.3, all of which govern charges on withdrawals; the closing proviso subordinates it to Section 1.4. Layered but signposted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The executive powers of the President in the event of a national emergency' is entirely undefined as to both the powers and what constitutes a national emergency. A short sentence with a large, nameable indeterminacy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside 3.3(a)'s and 10.4's emergency machinery, which require commission findings and unanimous or noticed action, and alongside 15.1(s)'s presidential power to delete plan provisions. Two emergency authorities over the same waters.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall serve at the pleasure of the President' is a definite tenure rule. No ambiguity in the words themselves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The compact's own Endnote records that this provision and Section 2.2 'were inconsistent as to the term of the federal representative's appointment', a conflict Congress cured only by repealing this paragraph in 1997. That is an acknowledged, documented internal contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A double-negative saving clause ('nothing... shall be construed as impairing or in any manner affecting the applicability to all Federal funds') whose grammar is broken — 'the applicability' of what is never stated. That omission genuinely obscures the meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves presidential and congressional control over federal funds, which undercuts 13.3(c)'s covenant to include apportioned amounts in budgets and 12.20(a)'s capital funding provision. The WRDA endnotes show Congress later legislating to force allocation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except to the same extent that state bonds are or may continued to be free or exempt' contains a grammatical error ('may continued'), and the sentence is a triple negative that is hard to parse. The intended meaning is recoverable but the drafting is defective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.8 exempts commission bonds from 'all taxation by or under authority of any of the signatory parties', and 1.2(h) makes the United States a signatory party — this paragraph is the express contradiction of that exemption. A named, direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Legally or morally' is an odd pairing for a disclaimer but its intent is unmistakable, and the subject matter is narrow. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 12.1's 'payable solely out of the properties and revenues of the commission' and 12.3's exclusion of signatory credit; it does, however, sit against 12.20(b)'s optional guaranty by a signatory party. Moderate-low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two sentences that reduce a pledge to a discretion ('pledged only to the extent that the respective agencies shall from time to time agree'); the language is clear, if one-sided. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly guts Section 11.5's mutual pledge as against the United States, so that the states' obligation stands while the federal one is discretionary — an asymmetry created by express override rather than by accident. Nameable and real.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long Davis-Bacon provision with an internal oddity: overtime at time and a half 'for all hours worked in any workweek in excess of eight hours in any workday or forty hours in any workweek, as the case may be' — the 'as the case may be' leaves the daily/weekly election unspecified. Otherwise the incorporation by statutory citation is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies to projects 'undertaken by the commission or... financially assisted by it', a broader trigger than 15.1(j)'s $10,000 contract threshold and than 14.9's bidding thresholds — three procurement-adjacent regimes with different scopes. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence incorporation of Walsh-Healey above a stated dollar figure. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The $10,000 threshold here matches 14.9's construction threshold but not its $2,500 supplies threshold, so contracts between $2,500 and $10,000 are bid but not Walsh-Healey covered. A deliberate-looking difference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A saving clause with a counter-proviso — federal water pollution functions are preserved, provided their exercise 'shall not limit the authority of the commission to control, prevent, or abate water pollution'. The clause and its proviso point in opposite directions and neither is subordinated. That circularity is a genuine defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 5.1-5.5, especially 5.5's preservation of state authority, and with 15.1(s)'s subordination of federal action to the comprehensive plan. Three provisions allocate pollution authority among commission, states and federal agencies without a clear hierarchy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Facilities operated pursuant to any other Federal law' is an undefined class — almost any federally regulated facility could qualify — carving an exception out of a mandatory bidding rule. Nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disapplies Section 8.4's competitive concession requirement wherever another federal law is in play, and the compact never says which facilities those are. A specific, identifiable hole in 8.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of statutory citations followed by a flat rule; precise in form, though the citations are dated and partly superseded. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.18 makes the commission liable for negligence 'to the extent and subject to the procedures prescribed by law generally with respect to officers... of the government of the United States' — i.e., the very FTCA provisions this paragraph says do not apply to it. Direct and nameable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical exclusion — 'other than the United States member, alternate United States member, and advisors, and personnel employed by the United States member under direct Federal appropriation' — is a four-item carve-out whose punctuation makes it unclear whether 'advisors' means only federal advisors. Modest but nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It denies federal-employee status while 14.2(b) vests commission employees with state peace-officer powers and 2.1 calls the commission an instrumentality of all signatory governments including the United States. The status of commission personnel is addressed inconsistently across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not be deemed to enlarge the authority of any Federal agency other than the commission' is a clean negative rule. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It calls the commission a 'Federal agency' by implication, while 15.1(m) says it is not one and 2.1 calls it an instrumentality of all the signatory parties. A small but real characterisation inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A jurisdiction and removal grant followed by an immunity reservation; both are conventional and precisely drafted, with only OCR noise in the section symbol. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It grants original federal jurisdiction over 'all cases or controversies arising under the Compact', which overlaps 3.3(c)'s Supreme Court original jurisdiction route, the various 'court of competent jurisdiction' clauses, and New York § 634's state-court definitions. Overlapping forums with no stated priority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short reservations of congressional power; both are stated in absolute terms and are clear. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The reserved right to 'alter, amend, or repeal this Act' unilaterally cannot be squared with 14.20's requirement of concurrence by all signatory parties, and 1.6(a)'s hundred-year duration assumes stability — the 1997 and 2007 amendments recorded in the endnotes show the federal power prevailing. A named conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At the rates which he shall deem to prevail in respect to comparable officers in the executive branch' is self-judging but administratively workable. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly displaces Sections 2.4 and 2.6, which provide that members, alternates and advisors serve without compensation; the WRDA endnote then requires the Corps Division Engineer to 'serve without additional compensation', reversing course again. Layered contradictions across time.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence carrying two provisos, the second of which lets the President 'suspend, modify or delete any provision of the comprehensive plan' whenever 'the national interest so requires' — an entirely self-defined standard — while the first imposes a 'shall not substantially conflict' duty. 'United Sates' is also a spelling error in the operative text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes federal action subject to the comprehensive plan while simultaneously letting the President unmake the plan, and it says Section 3.8 and Article 11 apply 'to the extent necessary to avoid such substantial conflict' — a materially different trigger from 3.8's own 'substantial effect' test and from 11.1(b)'s absolute expenditure bar. Reconciling these is a genuine construction problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The presumed-concurrence and withdrawal windows ('between the first and sixtieth day of the sixth year after the initial adoption... and of every sixth year thereafter') are numerically precise but the counting convention is not stated, and concurrence is deemed rather than given. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the mechanism for 15.1(s)1's concurrence condition, and periodic withdrawal of concurrence would unsettle 11.1(b)'s plan-based expenditure bar and 13.1's plan revisions. Coordinated but consequential.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The United States shall cease to be a party... except to the extent that the President deems remaining a party necessary and proper to protect the national interest' states an automatic exit and then makes it wholly discretionary — the two halves cannot both be operative. That self-contradiction is visible on the face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Automatic federal withdrawal would leave 2.2, 2.5, 13.3(b)(2)'s unanimity, and 1.6's duration provisions without a federal member, and 1.6(a) contemplates termination only by state legislative action. The compact has no machinery for partial federal membership.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All Acts or parts of Acts inconsistent with the provisions of this Act are hereby amended... to the extent necessary' amends an unidentified universe of statutes by implication, and the proviso then forbids the commission from 'repealing, modifying or amending any Federal law'. The scope of the implied amendment is unknowable from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 15.1(k)'s and 15.1(o)'s preservation of other federal functions and 1.4's reservation of congressional powers, so the compact both amends and preserves inconsistent federal law. That is a genuine whole-instrument inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such action as may be necessary and proper, in his discretion' is entirely open-ended but is a conventional effectuation formula. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors the identical Delaware, New Jersey and Pennsylvania effectuation sections; no conflict. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall cooperate with and furnish appropriate assistance' is mandatory in form but 'appropriate' leaves the content to the agencies. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It commands executive agencies to assist the United States member, while 15.1(h) says the furnishing of technical services to the commission is pledged 'only to the extent that the respective agencies shall from time to time agree' — assistance to the member versus to the commission is a fine and contestable line. Nameable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This Act shall take effect immediately' — three words, entirely definite. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.22 provides that the compact becomes binding thirty days after all five enactments, so 'immediately' and 'thirty days after' describe different moments for overlapping texts. The distinction between the Act and the Compact resolves it, but the tension is visible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All acts and parts of acts inconsistent with any provision of this act are... hereby repealed' repeals an unidentified body of law by implication; the class of repealed provisions is unknowable from the text. That is a nameable indeterminacy, though a very common one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeals inconsistent Delaware law while 1.5 promises to preserve existing state offices and agencies and 5.5 preserves state pollution authority. The general repealer and the compact's savings clauses point in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional effectuation authorisation; 'necessary and proper, in his discretion' is open but standard. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to the New Jersey, Pennsylvania and federal effectuation sections; no conflict. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Six words; nothing to construe. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same 'immediately' versus 14.22's thirty-day trigger point as the other enacting statutes. Moderate-low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The same implied general repealer, with the same unknowable class of repealed provisions. Nameable but routine.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeals inconsistent New Jersey law against the grain of 1.5 and 5.5's preservation of state authority; the same tension as the Delaware repealer. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard effectuation authorisation. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to its counterparts; no conflict. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This act shall take effect immediately'; definite. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same immediate-versus-thirty-day point against 14.22. Moderate-low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence — 'the powers... shall be performed by the alternate of said department head on the water resources commission' — refers to a 'department head' that the section never mentions, leaving the substitute unidentifiable. That dangling referent is a mechanical error that changes who may act for New York.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It implements Sections 2.2 and 2.3 by cross-reference ('the second subdivision of section two of article two'), correctly, but 2.3 contemplates only one alternate while this section creates a further substitute; and 2.4 provides for reimbursement of expenses, which subsection 2 here duplicates with a different funding source. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two subsections, each concrete: the mayor of New York City as advisor with a written-notice condition, and a named advisory committee. Little vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It invokes 'subdivision six of section two of article two' — Section 2.6, which is correct, since that is where advisors are provided for. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Consent of this state... shall not be given, except with the prior approval of the water resources commission' is a clean internal procedural condition. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites 'subdivision three of section three of article three', i.e. Section 3.3, correctly, and layers a state approval requirement on the unanimous consent 3.3(a) already requires. Consistent, if cumbersome.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It gives 'court of competent jurisdiction' three different meanings in three sentences, which is deliberate but makes the phrase's meaning depend on tracking which compact provision is in play. The cross-references are given in prose form, which is easy to misapply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies New York-specific meanings for a phrase used in 3.3(c), 4.3, 5.4, 10.6, 12.19 and 14.1(a)(1), while 15.1(p) grants original federal jurisdiction over all cases arising under the compact and permits removal — so a state-court definition may be displaced. Genuine cross-instrument friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean conditional bar on state permits where commission approval is required and not given. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its trigger — whether 'such project requires approval of the Delaware River Basin Commission pursuant to the compact' — depends entirely on the contested 1.2(g) and 3.8, so a state agency must resolve the same ambiguity. That dependency is real.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A power for municipalities to make aid agreements, with a saving for general laws; clear. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its cross-reference to 'paragraph (b) of subdivision two of section six of article six' correctly identifies Section 6.2(b), and the saving for general laws sits against 14.15(b)'s 'notwithstanding any contrary provision of law'. Small tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional bar on accepting delegations; the counterfactual test ('in the absence of the compact, it would have the constitutional or statutory power') is unusual but stated precisely. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites Section 10.1 correctly but restricts exactly the delegations 10.1 authorises 'as [the commission] may deem necessary or desirable', so a delegation valid under the compact may be unacceptable under New York law. That is a specific, nameable friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Departments, agencies and officers shall provide technical and administrative services... within the limits of available appropriations' — mandatory in form, defeasible by appropriations. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates New York's half of Section 11.5's mutual pledge, while 15.1(h) reduces the federal half to discretion; the asymmetry is created there, not here. Moderate-low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'During the ensuring fiscal year' is a plain misspelling of 'ensuing', and the rest is a concrete budget-submission procedure. The typo does not change the meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites 'subdivision three of section thirteen of article thirteen', i.e. 13.3, correctly, but subjects the commission's apportioned amount to review by New York's budget director, which sits against 13.3(b)(2)'s unanimous apportionment and 13.3(c)'s covenant to include the amounts. That is the funding-covenant weakness again.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete authorisation for the state comptroller to examine the commission's books and report. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its cross-reference to 'paragraph (b) of subdivision eleven of section fourteen of article fourteen' correctly identifies 14.11(b); it coexists with 14.11(a) and (c)'s other audits. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No provision of the conservation law or of any other law, which is inconsistent with the provisions of the compact shall be applicable' — the misplaced comma turns a restrictive clause into an apparently non-restrictive one, and 'inconsistent' is left undefined. The punctuation genuinely muddies which laws are disapplied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disapplies all inconsistent state law, which is difficult to square with Section 1.5's preservation of existing state offices, 5.5's saving of state pollution authority, and 14.19's saving of riparian rights — the compact's own savings clauses assume inconsistent state law survives. A nameable conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It twice directs that the compact take effect and be signed 'as provided in said subdivision twenty-one' of Article 14 — but Section 14.21 is Construction and Severability; the effective-date and execution provision is 14.22. That is a mechanical mis-citation repeated in the operative sentence directing the Governor's signature.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Section 14.22, which actually contains the thirty-day trigger and the six-duplicate-original signing and filing requirements, the cross-reference points to the wrong provision entirely. This is a specific, checkable relational defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This act shall take effect immediately'; definite. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits against 14.22's thirty-day trigger and against New York § 2's own direction that effectiveness follow the compact's own provision. The internal mismatch within the New York enactment is more pointed than elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The same general implied repealer with an unidentifiable class of repealed provisions. Routine but nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeals inconsistent Pennsylvania law against 1.5 and 5.5's preservation of state authority; the same tension as the Delaware and New Jersey repealers. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard effectuation authorisation, 'necessary and proper in his discretion'. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to the counterpart sections; no conflict. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This act shall take effect immediately'; definite. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same immediate-versus-thirty-day tension with 14.22 as the other state enactments. Moderate-low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An editorial endnote, not operative text, though it quotes two later statutes with ellipses and asterisked omissions that obscure the full rule. Its own words are explanatory rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly records that 'Sections 2.2 and 15.1(d) were inconsistent as to the term of the federal representative's appointment' and that the 2007 WRDA displaced Section 2.2 again — the note exists precisely because the instrument contradicts itself, and the reprinted compact still carries the superseded text of 2.2 and 15.1(d). That is a documented whole-instrument incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An endnote quoting successive versions of a funding statute; the quoted text is precise and the note itself makes no operative claim. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It documents that Congress had to legislate a duty to allocate funds 'to fulfill the equitable funding requirements of the respective interstate compacts', because Section 13.3(c)'s covenant and 12.20(a)'s disclaimer left the obligation unenforceable, and it still permits non-allocation subject only to notice. The endnote and Article 13 point in different directions on whether funding is obligatory.
